# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1–7 (Complete and Final – Updated 80)

## Setting and Time
- **Period**: Spring through late August of first year; Christmas/New Year period; nearly three weeks into new year (1832) just after Lords threw out Reform Bill; summer and autumn of first year; winter of first year; Vauxhall evening during spring of first year; spring of second year; summer of second year; autumn of second year; narrative extends into future years; present day with Fred and Mary at Stone Court in white-haired placidity
- **Primary Locations**: Middlemarch, Lowick, Grange, Freshitt, Mirecombe, Salwick, Quenwick, Fenmere, Bryngate, Chalky Flats, Gulton, Highbury, Cheltenham, Tipton, Yoddrell's farm, Frick, Miremere, Riverston, Quallingham, Halsell Wood, Loamford, Brassing, Stone Court, Coldcombe, St. Peter's Place, Lowick Gate, Shrubs, Dunholt, Yorkshire, Staveton, Bilkley, Harrowgate, Melspring, Wilhaven, Salford, Chiswick Mall, Hammersmith, Soho, Thames, England, Oxford, Chiswick Church, Buxton, Kensington turnpike, Russell Square, London, Southampton Row, Vauxhall, Exeter 'Change, India (Boggley Wollah, Ramgunge, Budgebudge, Calcutta, Dumdum), Forty Thieves theatre, King's 14th regiment post, Highbury Barn, Covent Garden Market, Doctor Swishtail's Seminary, Bedford tavern, Thames Street (City), Royal Gardens, Wilhaven, St. George's Hanover Square, Lambeth Palace, Great Gaunt Street, Queen's Crawley (Hants), Mudbury, Gaunt Square, Mansion House, Oxford Street, Swallow Street, Cambridge, Leakington, Squashmore, Bethesda Chapel Liverpool, Naples, Paris, Eton, Pumpernickel, Strasburg, Crawley parish, Yarlton, Quashimaboo, Fuddleston, Roxby, Wapshot Hall, Christchurch, Rectory House, Hampshire, Chiswick, Coldcombe, Huddleston, Cocoa-Tree, Woolwich, hill farms of Coldcombe, Humdrum Hall, Wattier's, Chatham, Horse Guards, Carlton House, St. Kitt's, Opera, Prince Regent locations, Demerara, St. Vincent's, Quebec, Charing Cross, Pall Mall, Old Slaughters', West Indies, Rochester, Chatham barracks, hill farms of Fenmere, Knightsbridge Barracks, Park Lane, Hants, Life Guards, 150th regiment depot at Mudbury, Dunholt village
- **Narrative Presence**: Narrator warns Vanity Fair is "a very vain, wicked, foolish place, full of all sorts of humbugs and falsenesses and pretensions"; observes human hearts and self-deceptions with ironic sympathy

## Main Characters

**Rebecca Sharp (Miss Becky)** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- Age nineteen; father artist/drawing teacher at Miss Pinkerton's academy; mother French opera-girl
- Small, slight, pale, sandy-haired with large attractive eyes; white slender fingers
- Skilled musician, linguist, artist; speaks French with purity; proficient in globes
- Determined, observant, capable of calculated charm; "I might go farther, and fare worse"
- **Governess at Queen's Crawley**: Governess to Rose and Violet; manages household; writes Sir Pitt's letters; won Miss Crawley's heart
- **Current Role in London**: Now Miss Crawley's companion and nurse at Park Lane residence; successfully nursed Miss Crawley during illness; displaced Miss Briggs and Mrs. Firkin from nursing duties; controls sickroom access; maintains composed, fresh appearance despite demanding care; never out of temper during illness; alert, light sleeper with clear conscience; tells stories about Miss Crawley's illness for entertainment value
- **Nursing Achievements**: Watched Miss Crawley's bedside with indomitable patience; nothing escaped her notice; found use for everything; Miss Crawley improved rapidly under her care; told imitations of Miss Briggs' grief that cheered the patient; doctors admired patient's improved state compared to usual depression; spent a weary fortnight in sickroom; nerves of iron, unshaken by duty and tedium
- **Relationship with Rawdon Crawley**: Captain Rawdon increasingly attached; visits her during Miss Crawley's illness; received bulletins from Rebecca respecting aunt's health; made confidante of his aunt Mrs. Bute Crawley; the "barbed shaft of love had penetrated his dull hide"; victimized by six weeks of proximity and opportunity; raved about her in "uncouth convulsions"; Mrs. Bute perceives his folly and warns him; she acknowledges Rebecca is "most clever, droll, odd, good-natured, simple, kindly creature in England"; warns Rawdon not to trifle with her affections as Miss Crawley loves Sharp like a daughter; Mrs. Bute advises Rawdon return to regiment and London, not play with poor artless girl's feelings
- **Miss Crawley's Devotion**: Miss Crawley demands Rebecca sit at dinners; would take medicines only from Rebecca's hand; quite overcome by little governess; loves Sharp like a daughter; would never pardon Rawdon for trifling with her
- **Status**: Successfully positioned as indispensable companion in London; has won over Miss Crawley, Captain Rawdon, and even Mrs. Bute (who initially hoped to hire her as piano professor); maintains control through charm and attentiveness

**George Osborne** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- Handsome brother of Amelia Sedley; believed by society to be infatuated with her
- Jolly, sociable; excellent at games, billiards, field-sports, song, parade; adored by men; famous drinker and sparrer; won Garrison cup
- Over head and ears in debt; known gambler, drunkard, profligate; shot Captain Marker in duel; robbed young Lord Dovedale at Cocoa-Tree
- **Engagement to Amelia**: Engaged; admitted engagement to Captain Dobbin and Mrs. Major O'Dowd; became furious upon learning regiment knows; upon reflection, apologized; admits "I am very fond of Amelia; I adore her"; acknowledges "She's faultless"; insists "there's no fun in winning a thing unless you play for it"; claims "the regiment's just back from the West Indies, I must have a little fling, and then when I'm married I'll reform"
- **Recent Financial Development**: Took tender leave of Amelia morning after visiting Osborne house; hurried to City; visited Mr. Chopper, his father's head man; received document; exchanged document at Hulker & Bullock's for pocketful of money; was "much too elated" to notice old John Sedley leaving banker's parlour looking dismal (FACT - timing suggests Sedley financial crisis coincides with George's gain)
- **Secret Liaisons**: For some time strove to keep secret; admitted "there was a woman in the case"; judge's daughter at Demerara; beautiful quadroon girl Miss Pye at St. Vincent's; reputation as "regular Don Giovanni" prodigious amongst young officers
- **Father's Demands**: Old Mr. Osborne wealthy merchant; has ordered George to avoid gambling or be cut off with shilling; warned George: unless Amelia's ten thousand pounds is settled down, George cannot marry her; states "I'll have no lame duck's daughter in my family"; claims Sedley's affairs look bad; instructed George to call on Mr. Chopper in City for money (COMPLETED)

**Amelia Sedley** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- Rebecca's former schoolfriend at Chiswick; spurned by discriminating sex despite school friendships
- Small, modest, unaffected young creature; tender heart; timid; sweet modest soul like violet
- **Relationship with George**: Confirmed engagement; believes deeply in George; innocent and trusting; assumes when George runs errands he is at Horse Guards, Chatham, or obliged to see friends; assumes he too tired to write long letters; loves George completely and trustingly; does not doubt him
- **Actual Behavior**: Leaves home daily; dines abroad six days week; neglected twelve dear Chiswick friends; single subject to think about; made confidante of little Laura Martin; promised Laura would live with her when married
- **Letters to George**: Extraordinarily long and passionate; filled sheets of large paper crossed with astonishing perverseness; wrote whole pages of poetry without pity; underlined words with frantic emphasis; repetitive; doubtful grammar; numerous notes followed him; ordered servant deliver only to private apartment
- **Recent Developments**: That very evening (after George received money) wrote him tenderest of long letters; heart overflowing with tenderness but still foreboding evil; asked what caused Mr. Osborne's dark looks; wondered if difference had arisen between him and her papa; noted her poor papa returned so melancholy from City, all alarmed at home
- **Status**: Unaware of George's actual financial transaction; continues to worry about her father's melancholy and Mr. Osborne's dark looks; remains innocent of George's true activities and debts

**Captain Rawdon Crawley** [CHARACTER]
- Captain in Life Guards; perfect celebrated "blood" or dandy about town; expert boxer, rat-hunter, four-in-hand driver; belonged to household troops around Prince Regent; fought three bloody duels; very large, six feet high; very generous with money
- Over head and ears in debt; known gambler, drunkard, profligate; all young men at Wattier's and Cocoa-Tree swear by him
- Miss Crawley almost adopted him; disliked Mr. Pitt; always paid his dueling debts; designated for fifty thousand pounds in will per Rector
- **Recent Developments**: Rode up from Knightsbridge Barracks after Rebecca's arrival at Miss Crawley's house in Park Lane; found Miss Crawley ill; found Miss Briggs in tears; Rebecca came down and gave him glance of scorn at Briggs; led him to back drawing-room; they talked ten minutes; parlour bell rung briskly; Rawdon came out curling mustachios
- **Current Status with Rebecca**: Got extension of leave on aunt's illness; remained dutifully at home; always in aunt's antechamber; Sir Pitt always meeting him there watching; both Sir Pitt and Rawdon anxious for news from Rebecca; Rawdon visits regularly; rides over to 150th regiment depot at Mudbury when leaving; completely victimized by love for Rebecca after six weeks of proximity; made confidante of Mrs. Bute Crawley regarding his feelings; she perceives his folly, warns him, but admits Rebecca is "most clever, droll, odd, good-natured, simple, kindly creature in England"; Mrs. Bute warns against trifling with her affections as Miss Crawley loves Sharp like a daughter; advised Rawdon to return to regiment and London

**Miss Crawley** [CHARACTER]
- Inherited large fortune from mother; silly and romantic; disliked Mr. Pitt; very attached to Rawdon; adores imprudent matches; approves Lord Nelson's character
- **Recent Illness**: Returned from Hants to house in Park Lane in travelling chariot; taken ill; messengers sent for physician and medical man; they came, consulted, prescribed; conveyed upstairs to bed in warmed chamber
- **During Illness**: Rebecca nursing her exclusively; improved rapidly under Rebecca's care; sat up and laughed heartily at Rebecca's imitations of Miss Briggs; became quite cheerful; allowed Briggs to see her; took medicines only from Rebecca's hand
- **Devotion to Rebecca**: Quite overcome by little governess; loves Sharp like a daughter; would never pardon Rawdon for trifling with her affections; orders Rawdon and Rebecca's proximity; facilitates their meetings

**Other Main Characters**
- **Dorothea and Will Ladislaw**: Married with infant son; established pattern of two yearly visits to Grange
- **Mary Garth and Fred Garth**: Inhabit Stone Court in white-haired placidity; Fred distinguished county farmer
- **Old Mr. Osborne**: Wealthy merchant in tallow trade; puffy, solemn, yellow-faced; instructed George to obtain funds from Mr. Chopper (COMPLETED)
- **Mrs. Bute Crawley**: Amiable, took great fancy to Rebecca; made confidante by Rawdon; perceives his folly regarding Rebecca; warns him appropriately
- **Miss Briggs**: Displaced by Rebecca; suffered same faithless treatment she inflicted on Mrs. Firkin; Firkin found consolation in Briggs' jealousy and suffering
- **Mrs. Firkin**: Lady's maid; eliminated from nursing role by Rebecca; came downstairs in tempest of jealousy
- **Sir Pitt Crawley**: Old, stumpy, short, vulgar; watches Rawdon's movements in sickroom corridor
- **Other Characters**: Mr. Chopper (George's contact), Captain Dobbin (George's friend), Old John Sedley (appears depressed leaving banker), Young Bullock (banker)

**Cotho Brackwood and Feena Stenworth (Dunholt residents)**
- Cotho moved to Dunholt from Mirecombe
- Feena followed Cotho to Dunholt within month
- Daughter born to Feena Stenworth and Cotho Brackwood; child named Thivie Brackwood
- Family lives in Dunholt village
- Thivie (child) told Cotho "You look tired," who did not deny it
- Cotho read almanac aloud, mispronouncing saints
- NOTE: This subplot appears unrelated to main narrative; purpose/relevance unclear

## Critical Facts and Status
- Rebecca now irreplaceable companion/nurse to Miss Crawley in London; has successfully displaced all rivals; maintains calculated composure and fresh appearance despite demanding nursing; plans to continue this advantageous position
- Rawdon completely in love with Rebecca; warned by Mrs. Bute to return to regiment; conflicted between attachment and advice
- Old John Sedley observed leaving banker's parlour looking dismal (timing coincides with George receiving money from his father via Mr. Chopper)
- Amelia unaware of George's financial transaction or true activities; worries instead about her father's melancholy and Mr. Osborne's dark looks
- Banker behavior changed regarding Sedley; staff exchanged knowing looks (CLAIM based on observation)
- Miss Crawley's illness has strengthened Rebecca's position and deepened Rawdon's attachment
- Young ladies lost governess instruction during Miss Crawley's illness; Rebecca's nursing duties prevent teaching
